answer: Per-identity entry toll with delayed refund. Each new agent identity must fund a locked escrow that only returns after a long voyage of verified, non-duplicative work, so a clone farm's capital stays trapped while genuine agents get it back. Every identity also draws from a shared grove of scarce compute slots, and a cluster of near-identical agents triggers throttling that strands their escrow longer. The oasis of profitable operation therefore stays out of reach for clones, since each marginal copy costs the attacker escrow float plus lost throughput that never repays.
